excerpt_byline: From the opening of Play — M. Patrick Furry
excerpt_body: Jack had given up on the word tired. The word had stopped meaning anything around month four, when sleep became less of an event and more of a rumor — something other people did, in other rooms, at appropriate hours. What he had instead was a long grey corridor of time that started at eleven and ended whenever the light came back. He walked it. He read paperbacks he could no longer remember the next morning. He learned which floorboards in the apartment creaked and which ones lied. It was on the long grey corridor — on the fourth or fifth or possibly hundredth night of it — that he walked past the storefront on Columbus Avenue and saw the neon sign humming, even though the building had been empty since spring.
